newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Tangshan Steel plans IPO of 120 mln A shares.
newsitem.headline: China Tangshan Steel plans IPO of 120 mln A shares.

text.p: Tangshan Steel and Iron Co plans to launch an initial public offering of 120 million A shares for listing in Shenzhen, a company official said on Wednesday.

The company has preliminary approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission to go ahead with the offer, which has been tentatively priced at 9.50 yuan per share, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The firm hopes to launch the stock in mid-March and has named China Guotai Securities Co as lead underwriter, he said.

Tangshan Steel, one of China's top 10 steel works, would use proceeds for a 2,500-cubic-metre furnace to expand steel and iron output. It produces an annual 2.2 million tonnes of steel and 2.1 million tonnes of iron for the construction industry.

Tangshan Steel, which became a shareholding enterprise in 1994, has about 1.2 billion outstanding shares made up of about one billion state shares, 168 million legal person shares and 32 million staff shares. The company, based in Tangshan city in Hebei province, estimated pre-tax profits at about 800 million yuan for 1996, compared with 700 million yuan in 1995, he said.
The company had paid corporate income tax at 33 percent over the past few years and expected to be assessed at 15 percent after going public, the official added.
